messages.author: d7fd273d0b8c973d
messages.subject: Hard stopping a run
parts:
Hello Nick and all,

Is there a way to hard stop a run and still get the results up to that point?

I have this one run that is going for a couple of months now and the likelihood does not improve anymore, but the run never finishes.

Cheers

JP

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: Hard stopping a run
parts:
Hi -- you can do this, just make sure you copy/save and write down all the parameters that have been printed to screen.  Then you will have to 

1. manually enter the best-guess parameters into the "init" and "est" fields of the params_table:

# if the maximum likelihood estimate said parameter "d" was 0.123

BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["d","init"] = 0.123
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["d","est"] = 0.123


2. Then, run the likelihood calculation one more time to produce ancestral states at that ML estimate:

res = bears_optim_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object=BioGeoBEARS_run_object, skip_optim=TRUE, skip_optim_option="return_all")

The object "res" will now have the same stuff it would have if the ML run had finished on its own.

Cheers,
Nick

parts:
Hello Nick, how are you?

I am trying to use your "shortcut" approach.

I am running the following R script and it goes fine until the test calculation of the likelihood. After that (about one hour using my personal computer), the run stops and the only message I get is: KILLED.

And there are no results or calculations.

Maybe something wrong with my script?

Here is what I am running:

setwd("~/Documents/R/BGBtest/shortcut/dec")

library(rexpokit)
library(cladoRcpp)
library(optimx)
require(parallel)
library(GenSA)
library(BioGeoBEARS)
source("scripts/biogeobears-utilities.R")

# Create run object
dec.potamo <- define_BioGeoBEARS_run()

# Check and import phylogeny
phylo.path <- "data/potamo_d6_fix.newick" # Tree in .newick format, previously generated
moref(phylo.path)
potamo.tree <- read.tree(phylo.path)

#plot(potamo.tree)
prt(potamo.tree, get_tipnames = T)

# Set tree in run object
dec.potamo$trfn = "data/potamo_d6_fix.newick"

#Check and import geography data file
geo.path <- "data/potamo_code_geog2.data"
moref(geo.path)
getranges_from_LagrangePHYLIP(lgdata_fn=geo.path)

# Set geography data in run object
dec.potamo$geogfn = "data/potamo_code_geog2.data"
dec.potamo$geogfn

# Set standard run config and rebind
dec.potamo = configure.standard.biogeobears.run(dec.potamo)

# Setting initial parameters for DEC run, free parameters = d and e #

### d and e for this run!! ###

# Input starting values for d, e
dec.potamo$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["d","init"] = 0.008
dec.potamo$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["d","est"] = 0.008
dec.potamo$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["e","init"] = 0.395
dec.potamo$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["e","est"] = 0.395

# Set max range size
dec.potamo$max_range_size = 5
dec.potamo$include_null_range = FALSE

# Inspect if model parameters are ok
dec.potamo$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table

# To speed up:
dec.potamo$use_optimx = TRUE
dec.potamo$num_cores_to_use = 4
dec.potamo$speedup = TRUE

# Set options to recover esimated ancestral states:
dec.potamo$return_condlikes_table = T
dec.potamo$calc_TTL_loglike_from_condlikes_table = T
dec.potamo$calc_ancprobs = T

# Confirm and check configurations
check_BioGeoBEARS_run(dec.potamo)
dec.potamo

# Run DEC analysis and save results
### THE FOLLOWING RUN OPTION IS THE SHORTCUT ONE!!!! ###
dec.results = bears_optim_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object=dec.potamo, skip_optim=TRUE, skip_optim_option="return_all")
save(dec.results, file="results/dec_potamo_lrun.Rdata") #make sure folder exists

Cheers

JP

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Re: Hard stopping a run
parts:
Hi -- I've never seen that error.  It suggests that the memory is at or near the limit on your computer (as does the fact that you ran the initial run for a month without it finishing, very unusual).

Perhaps either you've got a large number of areas, or a really massive tree -- google numstates_from_numareas on the Google Group, and read about the speed issues.

If that's doesn't make the issue obvious, try it on a bigger computer perhaps?

I'm on vacation right now, if you send not just the script but the input tree and geography files, and the information on your computer operating system, I could say more in a week or two.

Cheers,
Nick

Hi -- you can do this, just make sure you copy/save and write down all the parameters that have been printed to screen.  Then you will have to 

1. manually enter the best-guess parameters into the "init" and "est" fields of the params_table:

# if the maximum likelihood estimate said parameter "d" was 0.123

BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["d","est"] = 0.123
